answer: Thread-weighted action ledger. Each agent identity must anchor a minimal transaction thread to a shared ledger; the ledger charges a declining rebate only when a thread's activity reaches a fixed depth over a window. Below that nadir, every action pays full price; shallow threads gain nothing. An attacker mass-registering identities pays the full per-action tariff on each, since fake threads never reach rebate depth, so Sybil cost scales linearly with identities, not sublinearly as with onyx-shared pooling.
